verdict.tagline: Tactical brilliance wrapped in brutal odds and technical friction.
for_you_if: you accept heavy reliance on random chance
not_for_you_if: you cannot tolerate corrupted save files and crashes
you despise strict mission turn timers
you want a gentle learning curve

cohorts.n_note: n=14 - too few reviews to call

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early tactical encounters test resolve as permanent loss strikes unpredictably.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that characters can die permanently and squad members are easily lost due to random chance and critical hits.

citations.review_text: Got mind controlled on my first mission and lost half my squad in one turn.

The game seems great, it's just really not for me; this is a situation where I can't recommend it due to my own taste, nor do I want to tell fans of this genre to outright avoid it.

It's story telling within the small amount of time i've played, is spot on with lots of proper voice acting and world building- some parts doing a little too much "telling" rather than "showing," that being a small gripe.

XCOM 2 also includes a whole base/headquarters system where you can research, craft and manage resources, which in my opinion is a great touch and would have loved exploring the available possibilities that come a little later in the player's progression.

My main complaint:
I came into this assuming it was a CRPG, considering the turn based mechanics and a team you build and control. It does showcase a lot of what makes it to be, but the main discrepancy being the characters you control, are all capable of dying permanently in 1 - 2 RNG shots (early on but could also be later on too?), as well as not being able to build them through a stat sheet. I don't mind the exclusion of a modifiable stat system, as it's mainly handled by equipment and levels, but I do dislike the fact that it can all disappear because of 1 simple mistake or bad RNG. It didn't seem like there was any counter play for when a member of your team dies other than continuing the game while recruiting another expendable character, restarting the mission, or save scumming.

There's a lot of praise for this game, I truly believe the experience is great and worthwhile due to the communities' opinion. Going into this expecting the possibility to create your own team that you could stick with the entire time, and that there would be counterplays to possible permadeath, ruined the experience for me. I can't refund it because I bought it long ago, but I'll most likely give this one another try later down the line, now knowing what to expect.
Great game. Sometimes get way too attached to my soldiers just for them to die mid mission.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-campaign missions strain patience through sudden crashes and strict turn limits.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from crashes and corrupted save data that can erase hours of progress.

citations.review_text:
Fun game and all, but a crash set me back hours thanks to corrupted data. I doubt it's the games fault, but you know what is?

The game keeps deleting the saves that I manually do. Now when I loaded back to that uncorrupted ultra hard mission 2 hrs back, I can't load just 5 more minutes back to HQ and get upgrade my squad because the game deleted THAT save too.

This is the first time I had corrupted data, but it's not the first time the game has deleted my saves I needed it to keep.

Its a bit crashy and glitchy to give it a yes. It's a good game when it isnt crashing. Autosaves sometimes are corrupt so crashes instantly on reload. Have a character bleeding out (someone else posted they had problems if soldiers were unconcious but may just be a conincidence).  Its challenging on the esiest level, and with a luck based hit system be prepared to save constantly and reload constantly after misses or bad luck rolls of the RNG damage system. Level 3 out of 4 hardness I found impossible, and it was still frustrating at normal level. Only on easiest level do I believe this is playable without resorting to reloads to succeed so that's not really a game when you have to save and reload just to succeed imo.

Scale the luck more towards damage variation, or rebalance the difficulty. Then fix the crashing. Then the game gets "recommend."

Riddled with bugs, crashes constantly with only a couple temporary work arounds. 20 hours in and it crashes and wipes my saves at the same point every time. Unfortunately garbage game with tons of potential. But that's XCOM for ya.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience bugs related to line-of-sight and camera movement during enemy turns.

citations.review_text: Some line of sight bugs were absolutely terrible until I downloaded a bunch of mods. Now, the game is a ton of fun. Love it to death.

Waited a long time to play this game bc I loved the first one. I bought it with the War of the Chosen and I'm playing on normal and I must say, I'm not enjoining it so far. Yes there are a few cool new mechanics (like soldiers bond) and factions are cool but man there are a lot of cons.
The fighting system and the missions got worse compared to the first one...the percentage calculation is bonkers and everything feel off. The UI is buggy (I'm playing on a Mac atm), the camera, that used to be super cool is bugged as well and clunky; during opponents turns jumps around like crazy and a lot of time you will stare at a wall while an opponent overwatch shoots you through terrain and walls. In the first one I used to play without re-loading and just accept the losses but here, I've been reloading constantly because of the stupidity of some deaths. I'm still going to give it a chance and trying to finish the campaign but so far if I have to sum up the experience : TEDIOUS

claims.claim: Reviewers describe missing high-probability attack rolls as a recurring issue during tactical combat.

citations.review_text:
Flank the enemy, set up that perfect shot, and MISS the 95% chance. Don't worry, at least there's a sniper on overwatch that will MISS the 90% shot. Now the enemy has broken enemy lines and permakilled two of my best team members. Even if we succeed in the mission I now have to either train a rookie or pull from my good units to recoup a loss I theoretically had a low chance of messing up. 

Save scumming doesn't feel good when I can just repeat the same strategy and actually win because the RNG was in my favor this time.

Personally not my cup of tea.

>> This is not a strategy game <<
I'm a big fan of strategy and tactics games. I grew up on turn-based strategy. I have almost 100 hours in this game and I'll probably still come around to it here and there due to sunken cost fallacy. I beat it more than once and have enjoyed messing around with some mods thereafter. 
But I cannot in any capacity suggest or endorse this game. 

There are three main things that make me say this game isn't worth, going in order importance:

1 - RNG. 
A strategy game means making moves based on information given, a necessity being that the information is truthful. For example, in a typical strategy game there is HP, Def, Atk, etc. You make decisions on where to place your pieces and what they do based on those stats- you calculate, use your brain. That's the joy of strategy games. But any given stat for strategizing means ♥♥♥♥-all if RNG can decide that the stats don't matter. The trademark meme of XCOM is missing a shot when it's a 95% chance to hit (which indeed happens often), but that's just the first layer. 
The second layer is that RNG also decides how much damage you do/don't do (example: 2-6 damage on a shot). The consistency of missed shots is the biggest issue, however, as it really is the game effectively deciding that you just don't have a turn- worse yet if you position yourself to get a better chance at landing the shot. Imagine if you were playing chess and an unseen hand decided that you don't get to do anything for a turn. 
That's what it feels like. It's cheap, artificial difficulty. There isn't visible information about this happening before it happens, by design. It's a hidden dice roll of chance (which, by the way, is pre-locked, so if you save scum and do the exact same moves, you get the exact same results). It's not a strategy or tactics game, it's gambling. It's a slot machine. People like to gaslight about this and say it's the player's fault- Pay them no heed. It's purely sadistic self-righteousness.
In all s…
Played it so many times. You can't beat it for squad, turn based combat. You will often miss 90% shots but its still one of the best.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that missions include turn timers that pressure players to move quickly.

citations.review_text: Genuinely cannot recommend the game. The overwatch/reveal/concealment system is so inconsistent that it drives me nuts, as is the constant hurry in every single missions (all missions are on timer). Autosave is also one of the worst - whenever you load a game it overwrites your last autosave. This is incredibly frustrating. Yes, it's a good tactical game in itself, but it's not _fun_ to play. That's my biggest issue with it. First XCOM is worlds ahead of this game. I actually enjoyed and played through that one.

After hearing all the praise this game got I honestly expected much more. Good game sure, but the INSANE amount of downtime between everything that you do makes this game quite boring to play in long sessions 6/10.
+ every enemy is a serious threat
+ the base building is kinda neat (as well as the crafting and research...)
+ the clock makes every decision count

- since the enemies are such a threat, you have to kill them the moment they get into range
- like I said: downtime everywhere, 10000 animations, waiting for crafting/research to finish, waiting for the time itself...
- as the game progresses nothing really changes, your party is more powerful, the enemies have more heath, that's about it

I have only played it once, but I'm 90% sure that most playstyles are simply not good enough and the highest difficulty is hard in all the unfun/boring ways (Just a hunch). Every time I have finished a mission I just wanted to quit and do something else, the exact opposite of what you would expect from a fun and engaging game ("Just one more round, one more battle"), it is only enjoyable in short bursts.

i have tried many times to like this game as i played the older ones on hard and enjoyed it. But this style of rushing you all the time is not fun but just simply fustrating. no time to just enjoy the game. i have a life i use games to unwine not causing me to have a heart attack. remember before fan boys say anything i did like and played the other games on hard and it was fun. what a reversal of this franchise. even with mods it still does not make the game fun and on easy. The first game where even on easy is not giving you time to understand the game play so maybe you can replay on harder difficulties. really research this game before you buy it. I bought the game and all dlc.s and i will never play it.

The base game is already an incredible turn based strategy game. Every mission feels meaningful because every decision matters. Positioning, ability usage, resource management, and even a single missed 95% shot can completely change the outcome. (Yes, it will miss. It always misses.)

What really makes it special is how attached you become to your squad. They're not just units on a battlefield. They're your sniper who's survived since the first month, your Ranger who somehow keeps carrying impossible missions, and your Specialist who always seems to be one turn away from disaster. When someone dies, it actually hurts because you know exactly what it took to get them there.

Then there's War of the Chosen, which somehow takes an already fantastic game and makes it even better. The Chosen constantly keep you on your toes, the faction heroes introduce entirely new playstyles, covert actions make the strategy layer far more engaging, and the Bond system gives your soldiers even more personality. It doesn't feel like an expansion. It feels like the definitive version of the game. (Which it basically is since you have to launch it separately.)

While the game is no longer receiving official support, you honestly don't notice because the modding community has kept it alive in a way very few games ever achieve. The Steam Workshop is absolutely packed with mods. Quality of life improvements, new classes, new enemies, new maps, cosmetic options, complete gameplay overhauls, and even entire new campaigns. You can tweak the experience just a little or completely reinvent it into an entirely different game. It's one of the strongest modding communities I've ever seen, and it's a huge reason why people are still playing years later.

The amount of replayability is ridiculous. Different squad compositions, research paths, campaign modifiers, and thousands of community mods mean no two campaigns ever feel exactly the same. Even after hundreds of hours, I still find myself s…

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term commanders navigate complex technical hurdles and steep learning curves.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe experiencing technical issues including crashes, bugs, and corrupted save files.

citations.review_text:
I bought XCOM 2 collections years ago during a Steam sale, but my first experience was terrible. The game constantly crashed, was full of bugs, and even corrupted my save file, preventing me from progressing. After dozens of frustrating hours, I gave up and uninstalled it.

Fast forward a few years, after the 2K Launcher was removed, I decided to give it one more chance.

I'm so glad I did.

This time, the game ran smoothly from start to finish with zero crash, and I finally got to experience what so many people had been praising for years. XCOM 2: WotC is an absolute masterpiece of turn-based strategy. Every mission kept me on the edge of my seat, every decision mattered, and losing a veteran soldier genuinely hurt. The expansion adds so much depth that it feels like the definitive way to play XCOM 2.

If you're a strategy fan and skipped this game because of the old technical issues, I'd say it's absolutely worth giving it another shot. Underneath those early problems is one of the greatest strategy games ever made.

Now that I've finished it, I'm even more excited for **Star Wars Zero Company**, developed by Bit Reactor—a studio founded by many of the talented developers behind XCOM.

And finally...

**99% chance to hit is still not 100%.**
I really love this game but it has a nasty habit of waiting a few hours into a campaign to decide to screw you and your save file.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the user interface can feel clunky and difficult, prompting recommendations for UI mods such as icon color changes and resolution adjustments.

citations.review_text: Great concept and content. User interface is clunky and difficult sometimes but overall great game!

10/10 One of my top 5 games ever. One of my most proud gaming achievements is beating this game on Ironman Legend. The gameplay is extremely satisfying and rewards you for learning how to most optimally play. I almost gave up my Ironman run after a devastating loss, but picking yourself up and continuing on to beat the final mission by the skin of your teeth is a crazy experience. 

Great tactics, great story, great gameplay. The WOTC DLC elevates this to an even better experience. I would also download some UI mods such as icon color changes and resolution/naming changes.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the initial learning phase is steep and that the game does a poor job of communicating mechanics and tutorializing systems to the player.

citations.review_text:
X-Com 2 [WotC, as I've not played vanilla] is a very good game. It starts off very difficult, as the tutorial is... lacking, and the difficulty is the highest when you don't know the enemy, don't have many options to recover from mistakes and most importantly lack the experience to exercise proper judgment. Once you learn it a little, the game becomes easier, though the game does love throwing surprises at you at first encounters with an enemy (like the Muton counterattack, Andromedon suit revival or Sectopod explosion). Once you learn it more, the game gets quite a bit of depth, mostly due to the destructible environment. Block one ladder and destroy another, force a Hunter to break his legs repeatedly, Remote Detonate a train to cause a nuclear explosion after the enemy used it for cover, blow up the walls of a facility to access it easier, the possibilities are varied. Additionally, late in the game, there are just more tools available for tactical flexibility than earlier, like grapples, death from above, inspire, stasis and more, compared to just using a grenade to blow up a tree early on.

The Chosen are decently fun to fight. Knowing that they don't start their attacks until they're in actual fighting range is integral and, of course, not mentioned anywhere in the game. Spamming Mind Control is annoying, getting crit-bonked or bled out is also annoying, but not uncounterable... usually. The Rulers are bosses in every sense, when they actually attack, they deal the damage of a medium-high threat enemy, but with one action taken for every nearly one of XCOM's actions (Including ones that are not offensive or straight up miss). Devastate and Quake are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, Icarus Kidnap or whatever it's called is difficult to counter and why the hell do bosses that don't take cover have such high defense? I'd still recommend turning on the random mission Rulers, they make the game significantly more varied. The Lost, I could do without, honestly. Being punished for explosio…

Edit: TLDR: XCOM 2 isn't remotely difficult, it's merely punishing. And the things it punishes the player for feel completely arbitrary in a game that is entirely balanced around the AI being utterly incompetent.

Astoundingly sloppy. I considered this a well-regarded series, but I'm a bit surprised that people are willing to settle for this. The writing is utilitarian genre drivel, though that's typically what you might expect for a tactical game like this. The gameplay is the real focus. Unfortunately, XCOM 2 really ♥♥♥♥♥ the bed in this regard as well.

Depending on who you ask about it, you will hear both that XCOM 2 is brutally difficult and laughably easy. The latter is probably more true given enough experience with the thing. Because the game is dependent on a random number generator (RNG) to determine the outcomes of actions, the combat is incredibly swingy. Whether an attack hits or misses has a huge impact on the rest of the encounter (and the overarching campaign by extension). Therefore, it is paramount to mitigate the RNG whenever possible, generally resulting in one specific course of action being optimal. This won't prevent extremely frustrating outcomes, but "That's XCOM, baby!" The gameplay is actually pretty fun (for a time) once you get past the initial hurdle of the game doing an incredibly poor job of communicating things to the player. There are a lot of factors to keep track of, and Firaxis' methods of tutorializing are at once egregiously tedious and yet somehow insufficient.

The real issues arise as you become more and more aware of how badly implemented most of the gameplay is. AI behavior is extremely predictable given even the blandest of circumstances. Enemies really only pay attention to whether you're in cover and whether they can hit more than one target with an AoE (area of effect) ability. As a result the game quickly becomes aggressively boring once you're familiar with each enemy type, and no amount of arbitrary difficulty can f…

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that turn timers on missions restrict tactical pacing and discourage slow, cautious movement.

citations.review_text:
love the game, the mad scientist is comically insane. love the battles, the pressure, difficulty.
scored this on sale but totes worth it at full price. 
if you liked  any turn based tactics game, this is definitely a must buy.
oh- slightly buggy slightly frustrating, difficulty = possible to die even on the training mission.

bugs= enemies can see you when they have no LOS, they can see you high ground low ground, around corners, whatever, they have xray vision.  But if YOU are on low ground.... you can't see them.
the only way to succeed in some fights is to exploit the bugs in the system whereas the enemy doesn't aggro you if YOU don't see them...  confusing but basically you Must exploit that to win.  
And some fights you just can't win, you might get a bad rng and have 8 turns to run your troops a distance that is 9 turns distance away. or you might bug out and fail a mission even thought you finished all objectives. .. whatever still fun, oh and a  good fun combo is scouting with an invisible ranger, while your snipers shoot targets from 5 screens away with squadsight. =)

Every time I come back, I'm immediately reminded why I left it. The pacing and structure is obnoxious. It feels like browsing the internet without adblock. Having to move the entire base to a small remote area just to wait for some kind of supply, only to have a critical mission show up and force me to abandon it is just poor design.

Soldiers panic at a gentle breeze. An enemy can shoot at someone, miss, and a completely different soldier runs away screaming.

I like the idea of the stealth system, but having a turn timer on almost every mission makes it utterly pointless. I can't take it slow and outmaneuver the enemy because they're still magnetized towards my squad not matter how irregular my own movements are.

On top of all, the soldier's starting stats are far too low for the sheer volume of enemies encountered.
